classifications.one_line_reason: Timing/gating of a forced progress gate (level 30 vs 40) is a substantive flow-structure change a player experiences and weighs.
Adds/removes a feature (streak-saving item) that changes the rules of the habit loop; users consciously notice and value it.
Major layout/paradigm shift to a search-box-style widget changes how the user engages the core function.
Adds a whole content block of 3 extra paid offers; a present/absent section change.
Changes flow gating/timing by deferring a required field via a noticeable opt-out; users consciously decide to skip.
Reorganized layout that removes a content element (price); substantive what-is-shown change.
Changes the number of fields in a form; a deliberate effort/commitment factor users weigh.
Changes the number of steps in a flow (6 vs 3); a structural flow change.
Relocates an offer to a contextual moment with a cart-computed dollar amount; a deliberate offer/placement change.
Pagination vs infinite scroll is the canonical major navigation paradigm shift.
Adds a single line of persuasive value copy to an existing prompt; minor wording tweak, not a structural change.
Same-tab vs new-tab link target; below deliberate attention, the listed B exemplar.
Same box, but list content varies by browser/OS; cosmetic content reordering/swap users don't consciously attribute.
Color scheme inversion (black-on-white vs white-on-black); pure visual styling.
Single price vs a low-to-high range is a price-display formatting tweak, not a different offer.
